HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON movie still PAINTED like a premium digital painting, the look of a dramatic manhwa cover. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same confident ink linework drawn BOLD and THICK with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. MYTHIC PAINTED FINISH: rich saturated jewel-tone colour, never a muddy grey-brown wash; splashed sumi-ink spatter and dry-brush flying-white streaks breaking out at the frame edges; ONE bold sweeping painted ribbon of the scene's accent colour (cloth, smoke, banner, mist or light) carving across the composition like a brushstroke of legend. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. CHARACTER-INTRODUCTION splash, a dramatic manhwa cover two-shot. MEDIUM CLOSE. BOTH FACES LARGE, chest-up, filling the frame — the look of Sadaham's own intro card. SAME night Silla timber hall as that intro: crushed-black room, one oil lamp set down on the boards, paper lattice, timber pillars receding. Dutch low three-quarter. FOREGROUND, soft: the floor lamp flame, the king's red sleeve falling into the light. MIDGROUND: King Jinhung (LEFT face from the sheet — keep that bearded house face) mid-sit on his own timber step, thrown backward by his own throw, mouth open, comedy not dignity; deep red court silk, wide sleeves; on his head the OPEN Silla gold crown (narrow band, three flat 出 tree uprights front and over the ears, two shorter antler uprights at the BACK only, jade gogok, temple pendants) — NEVER a European spiked crown, NEVER a closed basket, NEVER horns at the sides, NEVER a black gat. The unnamed hwarang (SECOND face = Sadaham — ice-blue #6fa8ff silk, black crescent-moon headband, long hair, no jougwan, no helm) still on one knee, not looking up, the cup having just kissed the band. ONE device: a red-lacquer cup frozen mid-air on the way BACK toward the king, between their two large faces. #2f6fd4 as lamp bounce on the king; #6fa8ff as specular on the boy's band. Painted webtoon splash, NEVER photoreal. Faces from the sheet. No text. REFERENCE SHEET. TOP ROW, left to right: LEFT face = jinheung, SECOND face = sadaham. Copy each face exactly; give each person the dress the scene names. SMALLER SECOND ROW, left to right: costume chart (cut and shape only; ignore its labels, poses and faces), crown reference (shape only). KING JINHUNG — Look: Young Sacred Bone king: a round boyish face that never quite hardens, dark eyes set a little too wide, a short neat topknot under the open Silla gold crown. As Dharma Cloud: the same face, shaved head, no crown. Dress: Deep red Silla court silk, wide sleeves, a gold-trimmed sash. Out of battle he wears the kingdom crown. Late: a plain grey monk's robe, bare feet. Crown: Silla gold crown exactly as the attached museum photo (Cheonmachong / Hwangnamdaechong, 27 to 36 cm tall, as tall again as the face): an OPEN crown with no cap or lining, the hair and topknot showing through it. A NARROW flat gold headband (about a thumb wide) sits level on the forehead. Rising from it, THREE flat sheet-gold tree uprights, one at the centre front and one over each ear: each is a straight vertical stem whose short straight side-branches turn UP at right angles in three or four stacked tiers (like 出), every tip a small bud or heart. At the BACK, two shorter flat antler-shaped uprights angle outward with alternating branches, seen behind the tree uprights, never curling out like horns at the sides. Every upright and the band is hung on fine gold wires with hundreds of small round trembling gold spangles and many curved pale-green jade gogok. From the band at each temple, a long pendant chain of gold leaf-shapes falls past the cheek to the collarbone. Thin, bright, pale gold-silver sheet that trembles and catches light. NEVER a solid basket, never a castle battlement or fence, never horns or deer antlers curving at the sides, never a cap inside, never a European spiked crown or tiara. Colour #2f6fd4. SADAHAM Colour #6fa8ff. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark. NIGHT GROUND: the frame is built on BLACK — crushed ink-black night masses around the subject, the place pulled out of the dark only where the one key light (fire, lamp, torch, moon) falls, small warm bokeh in the black; the figure is the bright thing in a dark frame.
